label: rem:mass-energy-not-crossing-energy
title: Energy is not crossing energy
html:
The rest energy \mathfrak{E} = \mathfrak{m} \cdot c_q^2 (mass--energy equivalence) and the crossing energy \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} (crossing energy) are distinct quantities. No identity \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} = \mathfrak{E} holds across all braids.

Counterexample. The mass of a braid class is the framing-corrected trace (1+q^2)^n q^{-n-2w(\beta)} \int_A \rho(\beta) (mass identity). Take the trivial braid on n strands and a normalised Markov trace, \int_A \rho(1) = 1. Then \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} = 0 because there are no crossings, whereas \mathfrak{m} = (1+q^2)^n q^{-n} \neq 0, so the Legendre rest energy \mathfrak{E} = \mathfrak{m}\,c_q^2 is nonzero.

Why the two differ. The crossing energy sums q or -q^{-1} additively over individual crossings prior to tracing. By contrast, \mathfrak{E} arises from the Legendre transform (categorical Hamiltonian) applied to a traced holonomy observable, and the quantum trace [reshetikhin1991] is not additive over crossings. On two strands of the fundamental representation of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), with K = \mathrm{diag}(q, q^{-1}) and the braiding \check{R} normalised to eigenvalue q on the symmetric square, \mathrm{Tr}((K \otimes K)\check{R}) = q(q^2+1) and \mathrm{Tr}((K \otimes K)\check{R}^2) = (q^2+1)(q^4+1)/q^2.

Whether some auxiliary functional is simultaneously additive over crossings and determined by the framed trace remains open; one candidate is the logarithm of the framed trace, whose framing factor contributes the crossing-additive term -2w(\beta)\log q.
